about.text: An Argentine soft cheese defined in the national food code: whole or standardised milk is soured with lactic cultures and set with rennet, and the curd is moulded, pressed, salted and ripened for at least 20 days. The result is a high-moisture, fatty cheese with a soft, slightly acidic, white-to-yellowish paste.

how.label: cold brine
how.text: Large curd cubes, a light pressing and a short brining keep this cheese high in moisture. A brief cold ripening of three to four weeks leaves a soft, closed, slightly elastic paste with no eyes and a mildly acidic taste.

steps.note: A thermophilic starter was used in the trial.
With rennet or enzymes, after the lactic acidification.
Into a block or flat cylinder of 2–5 kg.
In a cold brine of 25–28 % salt.
At least 20 d for up to 2.5 kg, 30 d for 2.5–5 kg.
